value: > Having the doctor absent makes me somewhat pleased. Mrs. Carrow, my intention was to meet with you privately. label: History
value: Adrian was advised by his doctor to seek recovery near the ocean.
unit: Following a severe bout of typhoid, Adrian was advised by his doctor to seek recovery near the ocean. He traveled to the coastal area of Seven Gulls to view the old homestead of his grandparents, the Tremaynes. During his summer stay, he spent mornings writing and afternoons engaging in outdoor excursions, fishing, and boating with the Carrow family, Lorna Vane, and Captain Saul. During this time, he collaborated with James Garrick to write The Life-Book of Captain Saul, taking a photograph of Captain Saul that was later included in the volume. He fell deeply in love with Lorna Vane, though he wrestled in private over his feelings. After returning from his summer stay, he received word that his manuscript was accepted for publication. Later, while residing in Vancouver, he wrote to arrange another month's room and board, returning to court Lorna.

label: History
value: Ambrose Kerr was raised as a Grit.
unit: Ambrose Kerr was raised as a Grit and fiercely campaigned for the Liberal side during a general election fifteen years earlier. Confident in a victory, he publicly swore not to shave his face or trim his hair until the Grits achieved power. Because the Liberals failed to win for fifteen years, he faithfully kept his promise and grew long hair and a beard. He spent time going cod-fishing with Captain Saul and visited the lighthouse, where he entertained others by telling tales, singing Scotch ballads in an excellent tenor voice, and dancing with Lorna. When the Liberals finally won the election, he forced the barber Gus to trim his hair and beard before sunrise. He later married Winifred Tolley, and the couple settled into a comfortable green house.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia was named Jamesina.
unit: Aunt Euphemia was named Jamesina after her father James, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth. After her only daughter Elizabeth married and went to the foreign mission field in India, Aunt Euphemia moved to Portmaris to keep house for Nell Harcourt, Honora, and their friends at Tabby's Place. Bringing her pet Sarah-cat with her, she served as a housemother for three winter seasons, hosting the students and offering warm guidance. Despite a deep fear of snakes in India, she eventually traveled there to investigate her daughter's mission field.

label: History
value: Barney Pullen drove a double-seated buggy.
unit: Barney Pullen drove a double-seated buggy alongside his sister Odette to transport Nell Harcourt and Isolde to an event in Pale Sands, feeling immense pride in traveling beside Nell, whom he vastly admired. During a gathering with the local youth, he occupied a corner all night, observing Nell with a joyful smile. Having been given the upper farm by his father, Barney sought to marry Nell, but his extreme bashfulness led him to incessantly persuade Odette to propose on his behalf. After Nell firmly rejected the proposal, Barney quickly turned his attention to Nettie Scobie, whom he subsequently married, entering the Gorham Pullen pew with his new bride glowing with satisfaction and joy.

label: History
value: Belinda was born Leonora Bowman
unit: Belinda was born Leonora Bowman, the youngest of Mrs. Bowman's daughters. Following the path of her older sisters, she came to live at Echo Cottage with Miss Rosalind at age fourteen as a domestic helper in exchange for room, board, and clothing. Because Miss Rosalind routinely addressed her domestic helpers by the name of the original handmaiden, Leonora was dubbed "Belinda the Fourth." She diligently served Miss Rosalind, cooked, helped make clothing, and assisted with preparations for events. After turning sixteen, she spent time living in Boston with Miss Rosalind and her new husband, though she suffered from intense homesickness and expressed a deep preference for St. Brendan's Island. Later, she married a bricklayer named Tom. She returned to attend Nell Harcourt's wedding, where she happily helped throw rice and shoes to wish the bride good fortune.

label: History
value: Captain Saul spent his youth listening to his mother's seafaring heritage.
unit: Captain Saul spent his youth listening to his mother's seafaring heritage and reading poetry with the local schoolmaster, John Tremayne, before running off to sea. Over fifty years prior, his beloved Margaret was lost in a sudden storm, an event he remembered for the rest of his life. Throughout five decades as a mariner, he sailed across the world, once surviving a shipwreck on the Magdalen Islands and later tracking down a sailor in Havana whom he believed to be Rufus Vane. Five years before his passing, he retired from the sea and took charge of the lighthouse at Seven Gulls Point, choosing to stay there through the winters with his rescued cat, the First Mate. He maintained close friendships with Hugh Carrow and Nell Harcourt, visiting them regularly and participating in late-night philosophical discussions, story sharing, and music playing. With the assistance of Adrian Treleaven, his memoirs were compiled into a volume titled The Life-Book of Captain Saul. In his final spring, his health deteriorated rapidly, and he passed away peacefully shortly before his life-book was printed.

label: History
value: Cressy entered Wexcombe College as a Freshman.
unit: Cressy entered Wexcombe College as a Freshman, quickly becoming popular due to her elite lineage and charming personality. She introduced her friends Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis into various social circles across college. During her studies, she moved into Tabby’s Place as a housemate alongside Nell, Honora, and Mabel Colby, adapting to house rules and acquiring domestic skills. Courted by numerous suitors including Hector and Orlando, she met the Reverend Ezra Hale while spending a summer month at Prospect Point and fell in love with him. Despite her mother's initial disapproval, she successfully brought Ezra to her family home at Mount Holly and secured her parents' consent. Cressy earned Honors in Mathematics upon completing her final year at Wexcombe. She married Ezra in June, with Nell serving as her bridesmaid, and subsequently gave birth to infants while remaining in close contact with her friends.

label: History
value: Flossie attended school in Brierley under Miss Thorne.
unit: While attending school in Brierley under Miss Thorne, Flossie successfully walked the crest of the Pembroke garden fence after being challenged by Nell Harcourt. She became moody after being passed over for the role of fairy queen in a school dialogue, giving spiteful grins during public occasions and causing a three-month feud with Julia Bell by making a rude comment about her bow. At the local exhibition, she won the top prize for knitted lace. Flossie joined the Regent's class to prepare for entrance examinations, which she passed by a narrow three-point margin. She went on to attend Regent's Academy, residing at a lodging house alongside Frank Stockley and earning a reputation for being the most caustic-tongued young woman at the academy. Later, when Nell published a prize story, Flossie disdainfully accused her of plagiarizing it, and she continued to eavesdrop on telephone calls with her sister back in Brierley.

value: While attending Regent's Academy, Honora formed a tight-knit circle of friends.

During their subsequent years at college, Honora live at Tabby's Place on Linden Avenue together with Nell, Mabel, Cressida, and Aunt Euphemia. She excelled in her academic work, earning Honors in Classics upon graduation. Following her college years, she married a handsome foreign missionary and moved to Japan.

label: History
value: Hugh spent three years in Alberta.
unit: Hugh returned to Brierley after spending three years in Alberta with his ill father and a summer in New Brunswick. Re-entering school behind his age group, he quickly became Nell Harcourt's primary academic rival, eventually winning the graduation medal at Regent's Academy. When Nell sought a local teaching job to remain near home, Hugh generously relinquished his application for the Brierley school in her favor and took a position at Pale Sands instead to fund his future college tuition. He organized and served as president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society. Later, he attended Wexcombe College, where he was elected president of the Freshman Class, led the Freshmen to victory in the annual rush as football captain, and earned High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize upon graduation. Following a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he recovered and pursued medical studies. He eventually married Nell Harcourt and took over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Carrow.

Re-entering school behind his age group, he quickly became Nell Harcourt's primary academic rival, eventually winning the graduation medal at Regent's Academy. When Nell sought a local teaching job to remain near home, Hugh generously relinquished his application for the Brierley school in her favor and took a position at Pale Sands instead to fund his future college tuition. He organized and served as president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society. Later, he attended Wexcombe College, where he was elected president of the Freshman Class, led the Freshmen to victory in the annual rush as football captain, and earned High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize upon graduation. Following a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he recovered and pursued medical studies. He eventually married Nell Harcourt and took over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Carrow.

label: History
value: Isolde grew up at Pear Hill.
unit: Isolde grew up at Pear Hill and attended the school in Brierley under Mr. Pidgeon and later Miss Thorne. As a child, she established a deep friendship and solemn bond of comradeship with Nell Harcourt, with whom she created playhouses like Larkrise, invented fictional stories, and shared daily walks along the Aspen Path. Though briefly forbidden by her mother from speaking to Nell following a misunderstanding over currant wine, their friendship was quickly restored. During her school years, Isolde participated in the Story Club, sang encored solos at local concerts, and engaged in local social activities. Upon reaching adulthood, she joined the Brierley Village Improvement Society, serving as its treasurer. She became engaged to Gideon Duckett and married him a few years later, with Nell acting as her bridesmaid. Following her marriage, she gave birth to a son.

As a child, she established a deep friendship and solemn bond of comradeship with Nell Harcourt, with whom she created playhouses like Larkrise, invented fictional stories, and shared daily walks along the Aspen Path. Though briefly forbidden by her mother from speaking to Nell following a misunderstanding over currant wine, their friendship was quickly restored. During her school years, Isolde participated in the Story Club, sang encored solos at local concerts, and engaged in local social activities. Upon reaching adulthood, she joined the Brierley Village Improvement Society, serving as its treasurer. She became engaged to Gideon Duckett and married him a few years later, with Nell acting as her bridesmaid. Following her marriage, she gave birth to a son.

label: History
value: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls.
unit: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls as the intelligent and cheerful daughter of Frank Ainslie and Rose Kerr. Tragedies struck her youth when she witnessed her younger brother Julian's fatal accident at age twelve, followed two years later by discovering her father's suicide. Funded by her grandmother's legacy, she completed two years of study in one at Regent's Academy and became a beloved teacher at the Glen school. To save her mother from financial ruin, she yielded to pressure and married Rufus Vane, though she did not love him. After her husband vanished and was later returned brain-damaged like a child, Lorna spent eleven years faithfully caring for him in solitude while leasing her farm to survive.

label: History
value: Lucy was born.
unit: Lucy was born as a twin alongside her brother Robin Farrow. Following the death of their father shortly after their birth and the eventual passing of their mother, Lucy and Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters. Lucy adapted easily to her new household, assisting with small tasks such as feeding chickens, gathering chips, and drying dishes. While her twin brother frequently caused mischief, Lucy remained neat, calm, and obedient, sitting quietly during community gatherings and executing her chores systematically. During a severe hail storm that frightened the household, Lucy remained composed and silent. Following the death of Richard Farrow, a trust of two thousand dollars was left for Lucy and her brother until they reached adulthood or marriage, securing Grey Shutters as their permanent home. Over the years, she continued to be a dependable, cautious, and helpful presence at Grey Shutters, assisting with guests and young children.

Following the death of their father shortly after their birth and the eventual passing of their mother, Lucy and Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters. Lucy adapted easily to her new household, assisting with small tasks such as feeding chickens, gathering chips, and drying dishes. While her twin brother frequently caused mischief, Lucy remained neat, calm, and obedient, sitting quietly during community gatherings and executing her chores systematically. During a severe hail storm that frightened the household, Lucy remained composed and silent. Following the death of Richard Farrow, a trust of two thousand dollars was left for Lucy and her brother until they reached adulthood or marriage, securing Grey Shutters as their permanent home. Over the years, she continued to be a dependable, cautious, and helpful presence at Grey Shutters, assisting with guests and young children.

label: History
value: Mabel joined a circle of scholars.
unit: While attending Regent's Academy, Mabel joined a circle of contemplative and creative scholars alongside Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis. Following her time at the Academy, she worked continuously as a country schoolteacher instructing nine grades, an exhausting experience that inspired her to plan a realistic essay on the trials of a schoolmarm. Weary of rural teaching, she decided to leave and attend Wexcombe College as a Sophomore. She moved into Tabby's Place with Nell, Honora, and Cressy Lindsay, with her Aunt Euphemia handling the housekeeping while Mabel managed the household financial records. During her final year at Wexcombe, she participated in academic pursuits such as writing an essay for the Philomathic Society. After completing her time at Wexcombe, she eventually moved to Vancouver, where she worked as a teacher.

label: History
value: Nell was taken from Marden orphan asylum by Thirza and Obed Abernethy.
unit: After being taken from the Marden orphan asylum by Thirza and Obed Abernethy, Nell settled into life at Grey Shutters in Brierley. She attended the local school, where she developed a passionate academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow and formed a deep, lifelong friendship with Isolde Pembroke. Nell later studied for her teacher's license at Regent's Academy and subsequently taught school in Brierley while co-founding the Brierley Village Improvement Society. She pursued higher education at Wexcombe College, excelling in English and winning a prize for her creative writing. Following her studies, she returned to her ties in Brierley and married Hugh Carrow.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy was a farmer.
unit: Obed Abernethy was a farmer who lived at Grey Shutters alongside his sister Thirza. Seeking farm help as he aged, he and Thirza arranged to adopt an orphan boy from an asylum, but an error resulted in Obed picking up a young girl named Nell Harcourt from Alder River station instead. Despite his traditional fear of young girls and female company, Obed quickly took a liking to Nell's lively nature and insisted on keeping her at Grey Shutters. Over the years, he quietly doted on Nell, supporting her schooling, buying her a brown gloria dress for a concert, and taking pride in her academic successes, including her winning the Avery scholarship. In his later years, his heart trouble worsened, restricting his ability to perform strenuous farm labor. He eventually passed away, leaving a lasting legacy of warmth and kindness in Nell's heart, who faithfully visited his grave in the Brierley cemetery for years afterward.

label: History
value: Odette grew up in Brierley.
unit: Odette grew up in Brierley as the daughter of Gorham Pullen. She attended school alongside Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Opal Pettigrew, with whom she formed the Story Club. After passing her entrance exams with remarkable composure, she attended Regent's Academy and distinguished herself by winning top marks in domestic science. Upon graduating, she secured a position as a schoolteacher in Stonebridge, where she earned a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, though she privately found teaching tedious. While residing in Brierley, she actively participated in the local Improvement Society (B.V.I.S.), serving on committees alongside her peers. During a winter break, she reluctantly agreed to act as a messenger for her shy brother Barney to propose marriage to Nell, which Nell declined. After leaving her teaching post in Brierley, Odette traveled West to teach at a prairie school. While out West, she met Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman, whom she married in late May in a splendid wedding. Following her marriage, she remained unpretentious, happy, and affectionately connected to her old friends.

After passing her entrance exams with remarkable composure, she attended Regent's Academy and distinguished herself by winning top marks in domestic science. Upon graduating, she secured a position as a schoolteacher in Stonebridge, where she earned a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, though she privately found teaching tedious. While residing in Brierley, she actively participated in the local Improvement Society (B.V.I.S.), serving on committees alongside her peers. During a winter break, she reluctantly agreed to act as a messenger for her shy brother Barney to propose marriage to Nell, which Nell declined. After leaving her teaching post in Brierley, Odette traveled West to teach at a prairie school. While out West, she met Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman, whom she married in late May in a splendid wedding. Following her marriage, she remained unpretentious, happy, and affectionately connected to her old friends.

value: > Oh, she appears truly deceased. It fills me with fear, girls. Is it really proper for us to perform in this manner, do you think? Mrs. Sowerby claims that any drama-acting is dreadfully sinful.

value: > I will not be here Tuesday or Wednesday nights. A concert is taking place in Delford, followed by a gathering at Pale Sands. Herb Tranter is escorting me. He is my newest flame. value: > Because—because—oh, Nell, I am not scared that I will fail to get into heaven. I belong to the church. But—everything there is going to be so unfamiliar. label: Quotes
value: > I can’t help it. Even if what you say about heaven is true—and you can’t be sure—it may be only that imagination of yours—it won’t be just the same. It can’t be. I want to go on living here. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter and was buried in Brierley.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer relocated from Scottsford, New Brunswick to Brierley.
unit: After relocating from Scottsford, New Brunswick to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer purchased the western neighboring farm of the Abernethy place. He lived for a time as a bachelor with irregular household routines, employing young John Henry Carter to assist him. An early incident involving a stray cow brought him into direct acquaintance with Nell Abernethy, with whom he quickly formed a firm friendship. Though rumor once suggested he was courting Isabella Pullen when he was actually visiting Mr. Gorham Pullen for business and playing checkers with Mr. Pettifer Pullen, he eventually married Emily Scott in fulfillment of a promise made to his late sister. Following his marriage, he adjusted to his wife's compulsive housecleaning and social ties, though he maintained an armed neutrality toward Agatha Sowerby. In addition to his farm duties and delivering mail, he offered literary critiques and support to Nell when she began writing stories.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon served as the teacher at Brierley school.
unit: Mr. Pidgeon served as the teacher at Brierley school. During his tenure, he spent much of his effort giving individual instruction to older pupils preparing for the Regent's examination—most notably Sukey Pullen, whom he courted both in class and by visiting her home almost every night under the guise of assisting her schoolwork. He maintained loose overall discipline, allowing students to play and talk during lessons, though he occasionally struck children or punished pupils severely, such as making Nell Harcourt stand on the dais after an outburst and publicly mocking her spelling and geometry skills. Despite criticisms of his teaching abilities, he praised Nell to Obed as the school's brightest student. During a school Mayflower outing, he gathered blossoms to present to Sukey Pullen. At the end of his term, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to the school, leaving both himself and the weeping students deeply moved before departing his position.

During his tenure, he spent much of his effort giving individual instruction to older pupils preparing for the Regent's examination—most notably Sukey Pullen, whom he courted both in class and by visiting her home almost every night under the guise of assisting her schoolwork. He maintained loose overall discipline, allowing students to play and talk during lessons, though he occasionally struck children or punished pupils severely, such as making Nell Harcourt stand on the dais after an outburst and publicly mocking her spelling and geometry skills. Despite criticisms of his teaching abilities, he praised Nell to Obed as the school's brightest student. During a school Mayflower outing, he gathered blossoms to present to Sukey Pullen. At the end of his term, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to the school, leaving both himself and the weeping students deeply moved before departing his position.

label: History
value: Ezra graduated from Wexcombe
unit: Ezra graduated from Wexcombe and studied theology at St. Columbia. Although he resisted the idea of becoming a minister for a long time, he eventually accepted it as his assigned calling. Over a summer, he took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church, where he stayed as a roomer alongside Cressida Lindsay and four elderly women. He quickly became close friends with Cressida, enjoying boating, fishing, and moonlight walks with her. Despite initial hesitation due to his lack of wealth, he won her affections and later visited her parents at Mount Holly, ultimately securing their love and approval. They were married the following June. Later, he offered a wedding prayer at the marriage ceremony of Hugh and Nell.

unit: Ezra graduated from Wexcombe and studied theology at St. Columbia. Although he resisted the idea of becoming a minister for a long time, he eventually accepted it as his assigned calling. Over a summer, he took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church, where he stayed as a roomer alongside Cressida Lindsay and four elderly women. He quickly became close friends with Cressida, enjoying boating, fishing, and moonlight walks with her. Despite initial hesitation due to his lack of wealth, he won her affections and later visited her parents at Mount Holly, ultimately securing their love and approval. They were married the following June. Later, he offered a wedding prayer at the marriage ceremony of Hugh and Nell.

value: Robin grew up in East Welby.

He began attending school, sitting alongside his friend Milty Gammon and taking part in games with his peers. Over time, his behavior settled down, and he developed a passion for agriculture, eventually seeking permission from Thirza to take over managing the farm in the coming year.

unit: Rufus worked in his father Abner's store at the Glen in the winters and spent his summers sailing. He grew crazy about Lorna due to her beauty and pursued her relentlessly despite her repeatedly rejecting him. After her mother nagged Lorna into agreeing to the match to save her home, Rufus married her, establishing their residence on the Ainslie place. Quickly growing tired of domestic life, he left for Nova Scotia to visit relatives after Lorna's mother passed away. He subsequently embarked on a sea voyage to Havana aboard the ship Four Sisters alongside his cousin Laurence Vane. Upon reaching Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever. The ship was forced to depart without him, and Laurence stayed behind to tend to him until Rufus passed away from the illness thirteen years prior.

label: History
value: Tabitha Pratt lived as an unwed woman.
unit: Tabitha Pratt lived as an unwed woman from the Glen. She was hired as a general servant at the small residence of Dr. Carrow and his wife Nell. After visiting a sick person in the Glen, she returned to her duties and grew deeply devoted to Nell, affectionately referring to her as "young Mrs. Doctor." Though initially suspicious of Thirza Abernethy's arrival, she accepted her once she saw Thirza did not interfere with her kitchen duties or her care of Nell. She took pride in her cooking, competing in mind with Miss Tolley, and assisted Nell in hosting social gatherings. She also endured the presence of the First Mate, a pet cat, despite having little affection for felines.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters.
unit: Thirza Abernethy lived for decades at Grey Shutters alongside her brother Obed. Expecting to adopt an orphan boy from an asylum, they were instead mistakenly sent Nell Harcourt, whom Thirza decided to raise despite her initial hesitation. Over the years, she managed the household, taught Nell homemaking skills, and maintained a strict but deeply affectionate upbringing. Following the sudden death of Obed, Thirza continued to run Grey Shutters and took in the orphaned Farrow twins, Robin and Lucy. She faced deteriorating eyesight, though medical care eventually prevented total blindness. After Nell grew up and married Hugh Carrow, Thirza traveled sixty miles to Seven Gulls for Christmas, marking her first journey of such distance. She later visited Nell to support her during the birth of her child.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the school trustees of Brierley.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the school trustees of Brierley as the village's first female schoolteacher. During her tenure, she introduced novel educational activities such as bi-weekly recitation afternoons, field trips to the forest for nature studies, morning and afternoon physical culture routines, and strict emphasis on clear writing and simple vocabulary. She also instituted an after-school class for proficient students preparing for the Regent's entrance examination. Though her departures from standard teaching practices drew skepticism from traditionalists like Mrs. Sowerby and the trustees, she won the deep affection of her students and maintained strict discipline without ever striking anyone. At the end of the school term, her tenure in Brierley concluded after she accepted a job offer in her home district's grade school. She later visited Brierley as a guest, attending a meal alongside the Waces, Nell, and Isolde.

label: History
value: Miss Winifred was an only child.
unit: Miss Winifred was an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born. Her mother passed away before the boy reached three years old, leaving Winifred to care for him as both sister and mother until his death in his early twenties. During her youth, she had many suitors and could choose whomever she wanted. She also won an award for her lemon pies at the Port Marlow Exhibition. Along with other women of her parish, she took charge to organize, fundraise, and construct the Presbyterian church at Glen St. Agnes in six months. Later in life, she became a close friend and practical supporter of Lorna Vane, helping her around her home and defending her against neighborhood gossip. She regularly visited Nell Carrow and engaged in lively verbal sparring matches with her longtime companion, Captain Saul. Though known as a confirmed hater of men, she eventually agreed to marry Ambrose Kerr.

unit: Miss Winifred was an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born. Her mother passed away before the boy reached three years old, leaving Winifred to care for him as both sister and mother until his death in his early twenties. During her youth, she had many suitors and could choose whomever she wanted. She also won an award for her lemon pies at the Port Marlow Exhibition. Along with other women of her parish, she took charge to organize, fundraise, and construct the Presbyterian church at Glen St. Agnes in six months. Later in life, she became a close friend and practical supporter of Lorna Vane, helping her around her home and defending her against neighborhood gossip. She regularly visited Nell Carrow and engaged in lively verbal sparring matches with her longtime companion, Captain Saul. Though known as a confirmed hater of men, she eventually agreed to marry Ambrose Kerr.
